title: Occupied-office cleaning, shift handover and quality verification
audience: Cleaners and team leads running occupied-office shifts and shift handovers.
learningOutcomes: Plan a commercial cleaning route from the service specification, with zones, windows and exclusions.
Set up safe operations in an occupied office, including cable routes and public access.
Hand over to the next shift with completed tasks, exceptions and unresolved issues recorded.

instruction.heading: Reading the service specification
instruction.body: The service specification is the working document for the shift. Before you start, identify the frequencies (which tasks run daily, weekly or on a set cycle), the priority zones that must be finished before the office opens, the consumables the client supplies and those the business supplies, the cleaning windows when occupants are present or absent, the exclusion areas, and the quality criteria the client will use to judge the result. Confirm the site contact and the emergency arrangements for the shift. If the specification and the contract disagree, do not settle the difference yourself. Note it and refer it to the supervisor, following the variation process in the contract (see “Site contract and scope”). Build the route from the specification, not from memory of the last shift, because a route built from memory tends to miss the tasks that have changed.

instruction.heading: Safe operations in an occupied office
instruction.body: An occupied office has risks that an empty building does not. People walk through the work area, cables cross the floor, and staff are concentrating on their own tasks. Before you start, carry out a pre-start risk assessment for the shift. Name the zones you will enter, the equipment you will use, the walkways that will be affected and the people who may be present. Check electrical equipment before use: look at the cord, the plug and the casing, and check insulated parts for damage. The Code of Practice on managing electrical risks says that equipment should not be used where there is doubt about its insulation, and that insulated covers and mats should be visually inspected before and after each use. Remove any damaged item from use and report it. Plan cable routes so that they do not cross the public route, or cover them with approved covers where the site allows. Keep the public access route open, and place signs and barriers where a hazard remains. Wet floors are a slip hazard. The SafeWork NSW guidance notes that cleaning products and methods can leave floors slippery and that poor drainage lets liquid pool, so contain spills, keep the floor clean and maintained, and use wet-floor signs. Drying the floor as you go is working practice. Never leave hazardous equipment or a trolley unattended in a walkway, and coordinate with occupants so that confidential meetings and sensitive work are not disturbed.

instruction.heading: Working the route and verifying
instruction.body: Work the route in zones, and finish each zone before you move on. Segregate tools and cloths by zone, so that cloths used in washrooms do not reach desks or the kitchenette. A common order is to start at reception, move through meeting rooms and workstations, then the kitchenette and washrooms, and finish with waste areas, so that clean areas are not contaminated by later work. This is working practice, and the specification may set a different order. Verify as you go, not only at the end. Check high-touch surfaces such as door handles, rails and lift buttons, the floors, the waste areas, the consumables and the secured storage. Record missed rooms, spills that need a specialist response, and maintenance concerns such as a loose tile or a dripping tap. Use privacy-safe evidence. A photograph of a desk or a whiteboard may capture confidential material, so take photographs only where the site allows, and frame them around the defect. The quality check is the checklist, not your general impression of the room.

instruction.heading: Chemicals, SDS and the register
instruction.body: Every chemical used on site has a label and a safety data sheet. Before you use a product, check that it is on the site's hazardous chemicals register and that you can reach its SDS quickly. Use the product only as the label and the SDS direct. Choose gloves and eye protection to match the SDS and your shift risk assessment. Do not use a product that has no SDS on the register. Set it aside, refer it to the supervisor and record the hold. The Safe Work Australia guidance expects the register to be readily accessible to workers and to anyone who may be affected, so a register kept in a locked office that workers cannot reach does not meet that expectation.

instruction.heading: Shift handover
instruction.body: A shift handover is the point where responsibility moves to the next worker. Record what was completed and when, which access exceptions you met, which equipment is faulty or out of use, which stock is short, which incidents were reported, and where every key is. Write outstanding work in plain terms, so that the next worker can act without guessing. A damaged vacuum is isolated, removed from use, labelled and recorded in the handover, so that nobody reaches for it. A meeting room that is still in use is rescheduled to an authorised alternative time, and the rescheduling is recorded as outstanding work. Write the handover, and confirm in conversation any decision that was made at the end of the shift.

procedure: Read the service specification, and confirm the site contact, zones, windows, exclusions and quality criteria.
Carry out the pre-start risk assessment and check all electrical equipment before use.
Plan cable routes, keep public access open, and place signs and barriers where a hazard remains.
Work the zones in order with segregated tools, and coordinate with occupants.
Verify high-touch surfaces, floors, waste areas, consumables and secured storage against the checklist.
Isolate any faulty equipment, check the register for each chemical in use, and complete the handover with every unresolved issue recorded.

workedExamples.situation: During an evening shift, a meeting runs late, a vacuum cable is damaged and a washroom dispenser is empty.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do with each item, and what goes in the handover?
workedExamples.reasoning: Isolate the vacuum and take it out of use. Report it for inspection or repair, and do not use it to finish the walkway. Reschedule the meeting room to an authorised alternative time rather than cleaning around the people in it. Record the empty dispenser for restock. Put all three in the handover with the time of each event, so that the next worker can see what was done and what was left.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaning solution spill on the lobby floor blocks the main visitor route, and the next visitor is due in a few minutes.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the first action, and how is the route kept open?
workedExamples.reasoning: Place a wet-floor sign and a barrier at the edges of the spill, and contain the liquid before you mop it. If the route cannot be kept clear while the area dries, open a signed alternative route agreed with the site contact and tell the reception desk. Do not leave the mop bucket in the route. Record the spill, the time, the area and the action taken, and note whether the floor needs drying or a specialist response.

workedExamples.situation: A new washroom product is on the trolley, and its SDS is not in the site folder or on the register.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not use it until the SDS is available and the product is on the site's register. Set it aside with a hold label, and refer the question to the supervisor. Record the hold, the product name, the time and the person notified. Use only the products the register already holds for the shift, and say so in the handover.

equipmentAndPpe: Segregated tools and cloths by zone, labelled or colour-coded as the business system sets.
Gloves and eye protection as set by the product SDS and the shift risk assessment.
Non-slip footwear suitable for wet conditions.
Shift handover log and the site's hazardous chemicals register.
Note that PPE is the last control in the hierarchy of control. The site should first remove, isolate or reduce the hazard, and PPE supports those controls.

commonErrors.error: Leaving a damaged vacuum in a walkway to use later.
commonErrors.prevention: Isolate it, remove it from service, label it and report it.

commonErrors.error: Cleaning around an occupied confidential meeting.
commonErrors.prevention: Reschedule to an authorised alternative time and record it.

commonErrors.error: Handing over without listing unresolved issues.
commonErrors.prevention: Record every outstanding task, exception, fault and key location.

commonErrors.error: Using a product that has no SDS on the register.
commonErrors.prevention: Set it aside, refer it to the supervisor and record the hold.

commonErrors.error: Leaving a trolley or cords across the public route.
commonErrors.prevention: Plan the route, and place signs and barriers where a hazard remains.

commonErrors.error: Carrying a cloth from the washrooms into the kitchenette.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep tools and cloths segregated by zone.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Electrical equipment testing: the Safe Work Australia Code of Practice on managing electrical risks says that equipment in higher-risk environments should be tested at least every 12 months, and that more frequent testing may be prudent in some settings. Its examples of more frequent testing include commercial cleaning equipment every six months. Those are examples of prudent practice, not a general rule that commercial cleaning equipment must be tested every six months. The Code also says that equipment should not be used where there is doubt about its insulation.
Electrical repair, testing and licensed electrical work may be restricted under state and territory law. This lesson does not authorise any electrical repair or testing.

Hazardous chemicals register and SDS: the Safe Work Australia guidance says the register must list the hazardous chemicals used, handled or stored at the workplace, include the current SDS for each, be kept up to date, and be readily accessible to workers and anyone affected, at any time.

Slips and wet floors: the SafeWork NSW guidance (NSW only) lists spills, cleaning products and methods, and poor drainage as causes of slippery floors, and points to containment, floor maintenance, drainage and non-slip footwear as controls. Its order of controls places personal protective equipment last, which WorkSafe Victoria also states.

qualityStandard: Zone route (example: five zones) planned from the specification in the simulated shift, with zone order and exclusions shown.
Planted quality defects found and recorded, with location, time and action.
Faulty electrical equipment isolated and removed from use in the simulation, and not used afterwards.
Public route kept open, or an agreed alternative route signed.
Handover includes completed tasks, exceptions, faults, stock, keys and unresolved issues, without the next worker needing to guess.
documentationEvidence: Shift route plan showing zones, order, windows and exclusions.
Pre-start risk assessment and electrical equipment check record.
Defect log with location, time and action taken.
Shift handover record with completed tasks, times, exceptions, faults, stock shortages, incident reports and keys.
Register check record for each product used on the shift.
summary: Build the shift from the service specification, and refer any conflict.
Keep public access, cable routes and walkways safe.
Remove faulty equipment from use and report it.
Check each product's SDS and the site register before use.
Hand over everything the next worker needs, including unresolved issues.

knowledgeChecks.question: A vacuum cable is damaged during a shift. What is the correct action?
options: Use it carefully until the shift ends, since the cable still works
Isolate it, take it out of use, and report it for inspection
Tape the cable and continue with the rest of the shift

knowledgeChecks.question: A meeting room is still in use when you reach it. What is the correct response?
options: Clean around the people in the room, working quietly at the edges
Enter quietly and work at the edges of the room for now
Reschedule to an authorised alternative time and record it

knowledgeChecks.question: What must a shift handover contain?
options: Only the time the shift ended and the name of the last worker
Completed tasks, exceptions, faults, stock, keys and unresolved issues
Completed tasks only, so the next worker can plan the rest of the shift
